narrative.overview: ModelPick is staged as an optician's exam. Choosing a model is fitting lenses: the right strength for the job, no stronger. The page never looks like an AI landing page. The visitor reads a backlit duochrome chart that asks the question, types, watches the chart pull into focus, and receives a printed prescription. Two objects are lit and keep their colours in any light: the chart and the paper slip. Everything else is the room, a cool exam-room grey that dims to near-black when the visitor turns the lights down. The room is quiet so the two objects can carry the experience.
keyCharacteristics: A duochrome chart (red and green halves, black letters) is the heading and the signature.
Results are prescriptions on perforated paper, not cards.
Teal, the colour of an exam chair, is reserved for the one primary action.
Mono type appears only where a prescription would print data.
Dark mode is "lights dimmed", and the chart spills coloured light onto the room.

rules.name: The Two Lit Objects Rule
rules.body: Only the chart and the prescription slip own fixed colours. Everything else follows the room and changes with the lights.

rules.name: The One Teal Rule
rules.body: Teal marks the action you can take. Don't use it for decoration or headings.

rules.name: The Printed Data Rule
rules.body: Mono is for what a prescription prints: labels, numbers, prices. Sentences are never set in mono.

dos: Do let the chart and the slip carry the page. Keep the room quiet.
Do keep teal for the single primary action and selection states.
Do write labels in the exam's language: prescription, strength, frames, spare pair, your file.
Do respect reduced motion: no blur transition, no print animation, no lens hunt.
Do theme browser surfaces: selection colour, the red caret, focus rings and the scrollbar.
donts: Don't put a kicker or eyebrow label above a heading.
Don't truncate chip or button labels; author a short label instead.
Don't add same-size feature-card grids, gradient text, or glass panels.
Don't recolour the chart or the slip for dark mode; dim the room around them.
